title: Agent with tool-calling, not prompt engineering or RAG
reason: An agent was chosen because the system needs deterministic state mutation (intake, idea/plan status, step progression, activation) that a prompt alone can't guarantee, and idea/plan generation needs live market data via web_search rather than a static corpus RAG could retrieve from.
tradeoff: One LLM with tool-calling, not a multi-agent/orchestrator setup — one agent's loop covers intake, ideas, plan and check-in end to end without the coordination cost a second layer would add.

title: Three-tier memory split
reason: Hard state (current step, plan status, timeline, idea/plan status, failure pattern) lives in dedicated Postgres tables, always re-read fresh; the LangGraph checkpointer/Store is reserved for conversational context only.
tradeoff: Nothing authoritative is ever cached in or trusted from the checkpointer — more plumbing per tool, but no risk of acting on stale or fuzzy recalled state.

title: Tool boundary: LLM-backed vs. plain-code vs. MCP
reason: No tool that mutates intake/idea/step/check-in/plan/activation state is ever LLM-backed — generation (ideas, plans) and state mutation are split into separate tool kinds so a model's nondeterminism never touches a critical write.
tradeoff: generate_ideas/create_plan still perform their own deterministic Postgres write internally rather than handing off to a separate persistence tool, accepted because that write itself stays plain code.

title: activate_plan human-in-the-loop gate
reason: activate_plan pauses via LangGraph's interrupt()/Command(resume) before a plan can become active, enforced by a one-active-plan-per-user database constraint applied inside one transaction.
tradeoff: Adds a pause the user must explicitly confirm or reject before a plan ever commits — the cost of guaranteeing a human always approves first.

title: Moderation hook placement
reason: Mistral Moderation runs at three fixed hook points (beforeModel, wrapToolCall around web_search, afterModel) rather than being decided ad hoc per call site — jailbreak input is rejected, PII is redacted not rejected, unsafe output is replaced.
tradeoff: A cached web_search result is always the already-moderated content, so a cache hit never skips moderation — at the cost of moderating every result once up front.

title: Guilt/streak-language guardrail
reason: A separate, narrower afterModel check (not a Mistral category) catches guilt/streak-shaming language specifically, since general moderation has no matching category for it.
tradeoff: Regeneration is bounded (max 2 attempts) before falling back to a neutral message, trading a perfect rephrasing for a guaranteed exit.
